title: Scenes, choices and checks
summary: Scenes as data, option costs and d20 checks.
bodyHtml:
Scenes as data

A scene is a SceneDef (src/game/types.ts): id, kind, weight, regions, title, intro lines, optional talk, and options. Options carry an hour cost, an optional check, and results: any, or split by hidden truth (genuine, trap). Outcomes are lists of effects (fx.res, fx.hp, fx.nerve, fx.combat, fx.recruit, fx.scene, fx.end) interpreted by a small effect engine (src/game/effects.ts). Adding a scene means writing an object, not code. Text placeholders: {actor}, {other}, {a}, {b}, {leader}.

npm test validates that every scene, enemy, recruit and landmark reference resolves and that every option has an outcome for every truth.

Choices

Every option shows its hour cost before you pick. There is almost always a half-measure (leave water and a ration; send one scout alone) with a small cost and small reward, because the pillar is a spectrum, not a switch.

Checks

An option may carry check: { kind, dc, target?, exclude? }.

  • Kinds: persuade, calm, haggle, talk-down (charisma); spot, see-lie (perception).
  • The best-suited living member rolls d20 plus bonus against the dc, chosen deterministically by bonus (ties go to party order).
  • Bonus comes from role and trait tables in src/game/checks.ts, steady or frayed nerve, weakness, wounds, fever and fog.
  • The seeded RNG makes rolls reproducible.
  • The result { kind, by, byName, target, roll, bonus, dc, success, reason } shows on the outcome screen; option previews show who will roll and their bonus. Outcomes filter with needs: "success" | "fail".

The 3D client shows rolls diegetically (see Web client).
